Updated Mercedes SL Brings Back Proper Benz Grand Tourer, Report Says

MR
By Marco Rossi Senior Supercar & Aerodynamics Editor • via Carscoops Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Carscoops Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • With development led by Mercedes-AMG and sharing parts with the GT, the current R232-generation SL is a much sportier proposition than its predecessors.
  • While some buyers inevitably appreciated the change in philosophy, not everyone liked the SL's new performance focus , and the German brand is now being forced to return the car to its roots as part of a mid-cycle facelift.
  • Official reporting verified via Carscoops news desk.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • MARCO ROSSI Senior Supercar & Aerodynamics Editor

The Benchmark for Track-Tolerant Engineering

In the high-stakes supercar arena, pure horsepower is no longer enough to claim supremacy. This dispatch from Carscoops emphasizes how cutting-edge downforce balance, electronic limited-slip differentials, and hybrid torque-vectoring are reshaping driver engagement. Exotic marques must prove that extreme performance can harmonize with reliability, thermal endurance, and road compliance.

Big Picture: Lap times at benchmark proving grounds and early client allocations will reveal whether this performance envelope disrupts the existing supercar hierarchy.

With development led by Mercedes-AMG and sharing parts with the GT, the current R232-generation SL is a much sportier proposition than its predecessors. While some buyers inevitably appreciated the change in philosophy, not everyone liked the SL's new performance focus , and the German brand is now being forced to return the car to its roots as part of a mid-cycle facelift. The updated SL will arrive next year, and according to company boss Ola Källenius, it will be "more of a Mercedes-Benz."

📌 The Core Development

Autocar reports that Mercedes received feedback from buyers about the current SL leaning too heavily into performance. This insight is prompting the German brand to launch a standard SL variant with the Mercedes-Benz badge, rather than being branded as an AMG. It's understood the new version will include a unique front end without AMG's characteristic Panamericana grille. Mercedes-Benz will also tweak the suspension setup to give it a softer ride. Rather than carving up mountain passes, it should be more at home on long road trips and cruising along the French Riviera.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

While the new Benz-branded model promises to be more refined, that doesn't mean it'll morph into an uninspired GT car. Entry-level versions, including a new SL 500 4Matic+, are expected to use a turbocharged 3.0-liter straight-6 with 443 horsepower. This is slightly less than the outgoing AMG SL 55 4Matic+ with its 469 hp and easily out-muscles the 375 hp delivered by the old AMG SL 43 and its turbo 2.0-liter four-cylinder.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

Mercedes will also continue selling the SL in V8 configurations. These models will adopt the brand's new twin-turbo 4.0-liter M177 Evo V8 using a flat-plane crank that launched with the new S-Class. All V8 models will use some form of electrification. These could include a new SL 580 with roughly 530 hp, perhaps serving as the flagship Mercedes-Benz-branded model. Likely positioned above it will be a new SL 63 AMG 4Matic+ with 604 hp. Sadly, the current SL 63 E Performance, with its V8 plug-in hybrid and 805 hp, will reportedly be axed.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

Buyers in the market for a car delivering performance beyond what the SL offers will be wise to opt for AMG's more focused GT. Mercedes-Benz has been working on the refreshed SL since last year . Our spy photographers snapped it during winter testing back in March , in what appeared to be AMG and Maybach configurations. All models will feature a revised front end with star-shaped LED daytime running lights.
